Title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly being deployed as conversational assistants capable of performing complex real-world tasks through tool integration.This enhanced ability to interact with external systems and process various data sources, while powerful, introduces significant security vulnerabilities.In particular, indirect prompt injection attacks pose a critical threat, where malicious instructions embedded within external data sources can manipulate agents to deviate from user intentions.While existing defenses show promise, they struggle to maintain robust security while preserving task functionality.We propose a novel and orthogonal perspective that reframes agent security from preventing harmful actions to ensuring task alignment, requiring every agent action to serve user objectives.Based on this insight, we develop Task Shield, a test-time defense mechanism that systematically verifies whether each instruction and tool call contributes to user-specified goals.Through experiments on the Agent-Dojo benchmark, we demonstrate that Task Shield reduces attack success rates (2.07%) while maintaining high task utility (69.79%) on GPT-4o, significantly outperforming existing defenses in various real-world scenarios.
Major_Contribution_Result: The paper proposes Task Shield, a test-time defense that reframes agent security as task alignment: every instruction and tool call must contribute to user-specified goals. On AgentDojo under the Important Instructions attack, Task Shield reports ASR 2.07% with utility under attack 69.79% on GPT-4o (and ASR 2.23% with utility 54.53% on GPT-4o-mini), outperforming compared defenses on that setup. Ablations examine action-only vs input verification and feedback.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: Authors state: (1) if the defender LLM is weak or adversarially probed, extraction/scoring can yield false positives or false negatives; (2) the defense adds LLM calls for every assistant response and tool output; (3) main experiments use a single model family (GPT) on one benchmark (AgentDojo) and have not tested open-source backbones, so results are proof-of-concept rather than exhaustive evaluation.
Critics: Task Shield provides a concrete AgentDojo security-utility evaluation for indirect prompt injection, which is useful for agent-security benchmarking. Coverage is narrow (primarily GPT models, one benchmark, Important Instructions as the main threat), and the defense itself depends on a capable second LLM whose failures become the new attack surface. It does not claim system-level formal guarantees beyond test-time checks.
